title: Planning a wording bug gives it a check that reads the claim (wrong products absent, right ones present by name), not one literal phrasing
goal: SP-23m5etrf retrospective: BG-ab3tndhy's check required the literal 'Ubuntu 24.04' in the CIS summary; the goal research had already reworded it correctly as 'Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04', so the check failed on a correct text and a worker was dispatched only to repeat a product name. The kb-sprint plan step tells the planner to check a wording bug's claim by the items it names (each wrong product absent, each right one present in any phrasing), not by one literal string.

run: import sys; t=open('.claude/skills/kb-sprint/SKILL.md',encoding='utf-8').read(); s=t.split('## plan',1)[1].split('\n## ',1)[0].lower(); ok='wording bug' in s and 'phrasing' in s; print('plan step names wording-bug checks:', ok); sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
